projects.title: LCA Case Study: Sachet vs PET Bottled Water (Lagos)
projects.description: Designing a cradle-to-grave comparative lifecycle model to inform packaging policy and urban sustainability decisions.

drawer.subtitle: Designing a cradle-to-grave comparative lifecycle model to inform packaging policy and urban sustainability decisions.
drawer.body:
## Context

Single-use water packaging dominates urban consumption in Lagos, with sachet water and PET bottles serving millions daily. Despite widespread use, limited transparent, locally contextualized lifecycle evidence exists to guide policymakers, producers, and sustainability advocates.

This project developed a cradle-to-grave Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) comparing sachet water and PET bottled water using a functional unit of 1 litre consumed. The study combined deterministic modelling, sensitivity analysis, and Monte Carlo-style uncertainty assessment to evaluate climate impact, water depletion, and cumulative energy demand. Beyond technical modelling, the project translated findings into policy-ready insights and interactive decision tools.

## Research Objectives

1. **Develop a Transparent Cradle-to-Grave LCA Model**

  Constructed a full system boundary covering raw material extraction, packaging production, filling operations, transport, consumption, and end-of-life under Lagos-specific assumptions. The model quantified GWP, water depletion, and cumulative energy per 1 L delivered.
2. **Integrate Sensitivity & Uncertainty Analysis**

  Implemented scenario testing and Monte Carlo-style uncertainty ranges to evaluate robustness across recycling rates, packaging mass changes, and mismanaged waste shares.
3. **Identify Impact Hotspots**

  Disaggregated lifecycle contributions to determine which stages—packaging production, filling energy, transport, or end-of-life—drive environmental burden.
4. **Translate Results into Policy & Strategy Outputs**

  Converted technical outputs into policy memos, visual dashboards, and scenario tools to support decision-makers, NGOs, and sustainability communicators.

## Key Findings

1. **Climate Impact (GWP)**
  - Sachet baseline: 0.0425 kg CO₂-eq/L
  - PET baseline: 0.0897 kg CO₂-eq/L

   Sachet water currently demonstrates lower climate impact per litre consumed under Lagos default assumptions.
2. **Water & Energy Intensity**
  - Water depletion: 12.4 L (sachet) vs 82.6 L (PET)
  - Cumulative energy demand: 0.592 MJ/L (sachet) vs 1.912 MJ/L (PET)

   Sachet systems show significantly lower resource burden.
3. **Hotspot Drivers**
  - Packaging production is the dominant driver in both systems (38–56% of GWP).
  - End-of-life mismanagement significantly affects outcomes.
  - Transport contributes minimally under current assumptions.
4. **Policy Levers Identified**
  - Lightweighting packaging offers the strongest cross-system impact reduction.
  - Increasing PET recycling to 50% substantially lowers its GWP.
  - Reducing sachet open-burning rates improves performance margins.

## Overall Insight

This study provides one of the few localized, reproducible lifecycle comparisons of sachet and PET water in Lagos. By combining technical rigor with communication design, the project bridges the gap between lifecycle modelling and actionable sustainability policy.

It demonstrates how urban packaging debates can move from opinion-driven narratives to quantified, scenario-tested environmental evidence.

## Interactive Component

The project includes a Scenario Studio dashboard, enabling live adjustment of PET recycling rates, packaging mass multipliers, and sachet mismanaged/open-burn shares. This transforms the LCA from a static academic output into a decision-support tool.

projects.description: A research-driven media platform advancing sustainability understanding across Africa.

drawer.subtitle: Advancing clarity, insight, and contextual storytelling on sustainability issues across Africa.
drawer.body:
## Context

Susinsight is a research-driven sustainability media platform reporting on the intersection of development, climate, culture, business, identity, and policy across Africa. In a landscape where sustainability conversations are often fragmented, jargon-heavy, or disconnected from local realities, Susinsight fills a critical gap: it translates complexity into clarity.

As Co-Publisher and Editor, I shape the platform's editorial vision, build systems that support research-based storytelling, and ensure that every publication is insightful, context-aware, and accessible. I co-lead the growth of the platform from contributor network development to editorial frameworks, strategy, and long-term sustainability.

## What I Did

1. **Editorial Strategy & Research-Led Story Development**
  - Set the editorial direction and thematic priorities across sustainability, climate, energy, business, culture, and public policy.
  - Build research methodologies that convert complex issues into structured, insight-driven stories.
  - Guide deep dives, analyses, explainers, and newsletters anchored in evidence and contextual accuracy.
2. **End-to-End Content Management & Quality Assurance**
  - Oversee the entire publication workflow: ideation, research, editing, verification, design, and release.
  - Develop content frameworks that maintain consistency, strengthen insight quality, and uphold editorial integrity.
  - Implement multi-layer editing processes ensuring accuracy, clarity, and narrative strength.
3. **Contributor Network Building & Mentorship**
  - Recruit and manage a diverse network of writers and researchers across Africa.
  - Provide editorial guidance that helps contributors develop stronger analytical and storytelling skills.
  - Create structured contributor pathways, pitch systems, and feedback loops that improve output quality.
4. **Platform Infrastructure & Workflow Design**
  - Build editorial systems: weekly planning cycles, content categorization, SEO-guided strategy, and thematic scheduling.
  - Establish workflow tools improving collaboration, communication, and turnaround time.
  - Ensure operational consistency while supporting creativity and journalist autonomy.
5. **Visibility, Distribution & Community Engagement**
  - Shape Susinsight's public narrative through newsletters, visuals, social storytelling, and audience engagement.
  - Strengthen platform presence across key sustainability conversations in Africa.
  - Support partnership development with professionals, institutions, and organizations in the sustainability ecosystem.

## Impact

My leadership has guided Susinsight's evolution from a passion-driven idea into a structured, insight-focused sustainability platform. I developed stronger editorial processes, built a contributor ecosystem, and established clear research and storytelling standards that ensure clarity, accuracy, and objectivity.

Through this framework, the platform now maintains a pipeline of over 150 research-driven publications and has gained increased visibility within sustainability and development conversations. Contributors are equipped to produce nuanced African narratives, and audiences engage with accessible, evidence-based reporting that deepens understanding of the continent's environmental and socio-economic challenges.

projects.title: Kumat Services – Sustainable Energy Research
projects.description: Delivered technical research and strategic insights on clean energy, battery safety, and alternative fuels.

drawer.subtitle: Delivered technical research and strategic insights on clean energy, battery safety, and alternative fuels.
drawer.body:
## Context

KUMAT Services is a Nigerian automotive service provider exploring how renewable and alternative energy technologies can reshape mobility in Nigeria. As the country begins its energy transition, KUMAT sought research support to guide strategic decisions around battery safety, alternative fuels, and clean-energy integration.

I collaborated with KUMAT's research unit to deliver technical research, policy analysis, and strategic recommendations that connected global energy trends with Nigeria's local realities.

## What I Did

1. **Safe Storage Solutions for Lithium-Ion Batteries**

  *Focus: Battery Safety | Output: Technical Report*
  - Conducted a detailed review of thermal runaway failures in lithium-ion batteries—a major safety challenge in energy systems.
  - Recommended containerized storage systems to contain and prevent cascading thermal incidents.
  - Analyzed thermal characteristics and explosion safety to support next-generation storage design.

   **Impact:** Enhanced KUMAT's understanding of safe storage design, contributing to improved safety standards for energy storage systems in African contexts.
2. **Integration of Phase Change Materials (PCM) for Battery Safety**

  *Focus: Advanced Materials | Output: Technical Presentation*
  - Explored the use of Phase Change Materials (PCM) and battery encapsulation to isolate thermal incidents.
  - Proposed a hybrid model combining passive cooling and physical containment to prevent battery explosions.
  - Presented findings to KUMAT leadership, informing design improvements in containment technologies.

   **Impact:** Positioned KUMAT as an early adopter of cutting-edge battery safety innovations within Africa's growing EV and energy storage ecosystem.

   [View Presentation](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Z-nmb4JrpBDzG9IuRJ244D-akWbZyGYk/view?usp=sharing)
3. **Sustainable Energy Transition Challenges in Nigeria**

  *Focus: Energy Policy & Market Research*
  - Analyzed Nigeria's energy infrastructure, policy environment, and market barriers to renewable adoption.
  - Compiled an inventory of research materials and statistical data to guide transition strategies.
  - Proposed actionable pathways to accelerate clean-energy adoption within Nigeria's automotive industry.

   **Impact:** Provided KUMAT with a strategic framework to navigate regulatory, economic, and infrastructure challenges.

   [Read Report](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uV-QKpp6HJwk6U8iKvcJSFlIQ_Er_npK/view?usp=sharing)
4. **Employment Implications of Nigeria's Energy Transition**

  *Focus: Socioeconomic Analysis*
  - Assessed job creation potential in renewable industries versus employment risks in oil-dependent sectors.
  - Analyzed workforce transition dynamics and skill development needs in a post-fossil economy.
  - Developed recommendations for inclusive workforce adaptation during Nigeria's energy shift.

   **Impact:** Connected economic opportunity with environmental responsibility, informing KUMAT's broader sustainability strategy.

   [Read Analysis](https://medium.com/@toroadetayo/nigerias-energy-transition-could-redefine-what-work-looks-like-a978442704e5)
5. **Advantages of Propane Gas for Vehicle Power**

  *Focus: Alternative Fuels*
  - Conducted a full economic and environmental feasibility study on propane as a vehicle fuel.
  - Evaluated fuel efficiency, emissions data, and safety records compared to traditional gasoline.
  - Recommended strategies for integrating propane-powered systems into KUMAT's service offerings.

   **Impact:** Identified propane as a viable bridge technology toward low-emission mobility, expanding KUMAT's potential in the clean transport market.

   [Read Study](https://medium.com/@toroadetayo/how-propane-vehicles-are-quietly-changing-the-way-we-drive-3ed34fcf82df)
6. **Greenhouse Gas Mitigation Across African Countries**

  *Focus: Comparative Policy Research*
  - Analyzed GHG mitigation policies and implementation frameworks across African nations.
  - Identified best practices and adaptable policy models for Nigeria's automotive and energy sectors.
  - Synthesized findings to align KUMAT's objectives with continental climate goals.

   **Impact:** Positioned KUMAT as a regional thought leader in automotive sustainability and climate-conscious innovation.

   [Read Analysis](https://medium.com/@toroadetayo/the-rising-force-of-african-climate-solutions-5eb0070445c8)
7. **Energy Storage Research & Publication**

  *Focus: Academic Research | Output: Journal Paper (2024)*
  - Authored a comprehensive review paper on lithium-ion battery safety and thermal management.
  - Synthesized global research findings into actionable insights for both academic and industry audiences.
  - Strengthened KUMAT's knowledge base in energy storage system design and innovation.

   **Impact:** Contributed to academic and industrial understanding of battery safety technologies, reinforcing KUMAT's position at the forefront of sustainable energy research in Africa.

   [Read Publication](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VGhSl5J2EbbGbRvxM6GqMhhiadGlHUg1/view)

## Overall Impact

During my tenure with KUMAT, I helped guide the company's evolution toward cleaner, safer, and more sustainable energy technologies. My research bridged technical innovation with strategic decision-making—empowering KUMAT to align its automotive services with Africa's ongoing energy transition.

projects.title: Innovative Continuous Regeneration of Phenolic Resin Carbons for Water Treatment
projects.description: Developing an advanced carbon regeneration system for sustainable large-scale water treatment.

drawer.subtitle: Developing an advanced carbon regeneration system for sustainable large-scale water treatment.
drawer.body:
## Context

Micropollutants—such as pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and persistent organic chemicals—pose a growing threat to global water systems. Traditional water-treatment technologies, especially fixed-bed Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) systems, often struggle to effectively remove highly polar or water-soluble contaminants.

This project explored a next-generation adsorption process using continuous moving-bed systems combined with in-situ steam regeneration—aiming to develop a more efficient, sustainable, and cost-effective alternative to conventional carbon filters.

The work focused specifically on removing metaldehyde, a notoriously persistent pollutant, using Phenolic Resin Carbon (PRC) as the adsorbent.

## Research Objectives

1. **Develop a Process Model for PRCs**

  Created a mathematical model integrating moving-bed adsorption and in-situ steam regeneration to optimize carbon use, regeneration efficiency, and breakthrough performance.
2. **Design a Detailed Process Flow Diagram (PFD)**

  Mapped carbon circulation rates, steam requirements, condensate treatment, regeneration temperature profiles, and carbon recycling loops.
3. **Conduct an Economic Analysis**

  Evaluated the financial viability of the intensified process compared to conventional GAC filters, considering capital and operating costs.
4. **Perform a Lifecycle Assessment (LCA)**

  Used openLCA to compare the environmental impacts of the intensified system vs. traditional fixed-bed systems across energy, materials, and long-term sustainability metrics.

## Key Findings

1. **Breakthrough & System Performance**
  - Optimal breakthrough conditions occurred at a linear velocity of 10.8 m/h and bed height of 10 m.
  - Best performance for PRC adsorption was achieved with a 7.5% carbon recirculation rate.
2. **Regeneration & Steam Consumption**
  - In-situ steam regeneration at 200°C proved effective for metaldehyde removal.
  - Steam consumption was significantly lower than expected due to low pollutant concentrations, high adsorptive capacity of PRC, and efficient process-intensified design.
3. **Economic & Environmental Benefits**

  The Process-Intensified (PI) system outperformed traditional carbon filters in operational cost savings, energy efficiency, lifecycle environmental impact, and carbon utilization efficiency.

## Overall Impact

The intensified moving-bed adsorption system is a technically superior, economically viable, and environmentally sustainable alternative to conventional fixed-bed GAC systems for micropollutant removal.

This research contributes to advancing water-treatment infrastructure that is adaptable, scalable, and aligned with global sustainability goals.

projects.title: Life Cycle Assessment of Car Transport in Nigeria
projects.description: Evaluating the environmental impacts of diesel and petrol vehicles within Nigeria's transport ecosystem.

drawer.subtitle: Evaluating the environmental impacts of diesel and petrol vehicles within Nigeria's transport ecosystem.
drawer.body:
## Context

Nigeria's transportation sector is overwhelmingly dependent on fossil fuels, making it a major contributor to air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. With a rapidly growing population and tens of thousands of new vehicles entering the market each year, understanding the environmental burden of petrol and diesel cars has become essential.

This project applied Lifecycle Assessment (LCA) to compare the cradle-to-grave environmental impacts of diesel and petrol vehicles in Nigeria—spanning vehicle manufacturing, fuel production, and real-world operation.

## Research Objectives

1. **Build a Comprehensive Impact Inventory**

  Developed an extensive dataset detailing:
  - Emissions from fuel extraction and refining
  - Vehicle manufacturing impacts
  - Operational emissions from diesel and petrol engines
  - Resource consumption and energy use across the lifecycle
2. **Compare Diesel vs. Petrol Vehicle Impacts**

  Performed a rigorous LCA comparing both vehicle types based on:
  - Greenhouse gas emissions
  - Air pollutants
  - Energy demand
  - Overall ecological footprint

   The analysis followed ISO 14044:2006 standards to ensure methodological rigor.

## Key Findings

1. **Diesel Vehicles**
  - More fuel-efficient than petrol cars
  - Higher emissions of harmful pollutants
  - Greater overall greenhouse gas impact in the Nigerian context
2. **Petrol Vehicles**
  - Lower overall emissions intensity
  - Still significant contributors to Nigeria's transport-sector pollution

## Overall Insight

Despite efficiency advantages, diesel vehicles were shown to have larger environmental burdens, highlighting the need for cleaner alternatives such as natural gas, propane, hybrid systems, or electric mobility (where feasible).

## Implications for Nigeria

The findings provide valuable insights for:

- Government agencies: informing policy on fuel standards and emissions regulation
- Transport companies: guiding fleet transition strategies
- Automotive manufacturers and importers: supporting cleaner vehicle portfolios
- Researchers and sustainability planners: enabling evidence-based decision-making

The report emphasizes the importance of shifting away from traditional petroleum fuels to align with global climate goals and Nigeria's sustainability ambitions.

## Context

The AR Initiative is a Lagos-based sustainability consultancy helping African startups and SMEs embed environmental, social, and governance (ESG) principles into their operations. As sustainability reporting becomes essential for investment and growth, The AR Initiative bridges the gap between global frameworks and local realities.

I supported research and advisory work across multiple sectors—helping businesses align with ESG standards, assess their impact, and develop actionable sustainability strategies.

## What I Did

1. **Transforming Africa: Tackling Carbon Intensity**

  *Type: White Paper | Client: Ambo Ventures*
  - Researched Nigeria's most carbon-intensive industries (food, transport, energy) and their impact on biodiversity.
  - Conducted industry assessments, expert interviews, and data visualization to inform climate-conscious policies.
  - Developed policy recommendations tailored to Nigeria's context, guiding Ambo Ventures' $50M socially responsible investment strategy.
  - Delivered actionable insights to help SMEs adopt low-carbon, biodiversity-friendly business models.

   **Impact:** Provided a foundational framework for sustainable investment across Africa's high-emission sectors, influencing green policy dialogues and sectoral reform.
2. **Empowering Farms with Data-Driven Sustainability**

  *Type: Impact Report | Client: Farmz2U (Agric-Tech)*
  - Designed custom sustainability disclosure questions focused on soil health, aligned with GRI Standards.
  - Enhanced Farmz2U's data collection on environmental performance in Nigeria's agricultural technology sector.
  - Helped the company establish measurable metrics to monitor soil quality and sustainable farming outcomes.

   **Impact:** Enabled Farmz2U to embed sustainability reporting into operations, positioning the startup as a leader in data-driven sustainable agriculture in Africa.
3. **Empowering Education for Africa**

  *Type: Impact Report | Client: Teesas (Ed-Tech)*
  - Developed a materiality map identifying key sustainability priorities: inclusion, retention, and educational quality.
  - Conducted stakeholder interviews and performance analysis to assess social and environmental outcomes.
  - Recommended strategies to improve accessibility, community involvement, and educational impact.

   **Impact:** Informed Teesas' sustainability strategy, ensuring its growth aligns with inclusive, socially responsible education practices.
4. **Transforming Healthcare in Africa**

  *Type: Impact Report | Client: Healthtracka (Health-Tech)*
  - Created a GRI-aligned sustainability framework covering economic, environmental, and social dimensions.
  - Evaluated key metrics such as waste management, procurement practices, and data privacy.
  - Developed recommendations to enhance operational sustainability and stakeholder engagement.

   **Impact:** Strengthened Healthtracka's ESG performance and established it as a responsible leader in Africa's digital healthcare ecosystem.
5. **Revving Up Nigeria's Green Transit**

  *Type: Research Survey | Cities: Lagos & Abuja*
  - Co-led a nationwide survey and emissions analysis on Nigeria's transportation sector.
  - Designed and executed stakeholder surveys with drivers, automakers, and policy actors.
  - Identified key challenges in outdated vehicle fleets and emissions intensity.
  - Proposed sustainable urban mobility strategies and policy frameworks for green transport.

   **Impact:** Produced one of Nigeria's early data-driven reports on transportation emissions, guiding urban sustainability policy discussions in Lagos and Abuja.

## Overall Impact

Through these projects, I helped bridge the gap between sustainability theory and actionable practice—supporting African startups and SMEs to operate responsibly, align with ESG standards, and drive measurable social and environmental change.

drawer.subtitle: Investigating nonprofit impact and building a communications strategy for One Acre Fund's 2023 activities.
drawer.body:
## Context

One Acre Fund is a nonprofit organization supporting smallholder farmers across sub-Saharan Africa with financing, training, and market access to improve yields, income, and food security.

This personal research project involved developing a comprehensive impact assessment of One Acre Fund's 2023 activities, alongside a communication strategy to distribute and position the report effectively. The goal was to evaluate the organization's scale, progress, and achievements, and to translate those insights into a clear, compelling narrative for stakeholders.

## Project Purpose

- Assess One Acre Fund's reach, impact, and performance across sub-Saharan Africa.
- Distill organizational achievements into a structured, data-driven report.
- Develop a communication plan for effectively sharing the report with donors, partners, and the public.
- Strengthen skills in sustainability reporting, nonprofit analysis, and strategic communication.

## Key Areas of Focus

The report examined One Acre Fund's performance through:

- Program scale and reach
- Financial sustainability
- Innovation in agricultural support
- Climate resilience initiatives
- Farmer livelihoods and community benefits

## Highlights From the 2023 Impact Review

1. **Organizational Reach & Beneficiaries**
  - 4.8 million farmers served across nine African countries.
  - 26 million farm family members reached indirectly.
  - Expansion of agroforestry programs supporting large-scale tree planting and soil restoration.
2. **Financial Strength & Sustainability**
  - Over $100 million in donor funding and grants raised.
  - Sustained 95% loan repayment rate, demonstrating strong farmer trust and program value.
3. **Climate & Risk Innovation**
  - Launched One Acre Fund Re, a reinsurance facility providing low-cost protection against extreme weather.
  - Expanded climate-smart farming practices to help farmers adapt to volatile climate patterns.
4. **Digital Transformation**
  - Rolled out new digital tools for farmer training and remote support.
  - Increased access to agronomic knowledge through mobile-based learning resources.

## What I Delivered

### Impact Report (Primary Output)

A structured, evidence-based document that:

- Synthesized One Acre Fund's 2023 achievements.
- Highlighted performance metrics and key milestones.
- Explained the importance of the organization's mission and long-term strategy.
- Positioned the organization within the broader context of African agriculture and food security.

### Communication Plan (Secondary Output)

A strategic dissemination plan that included:

- Target audience segmentation (donors, policymakers, partners, the public).
- Tailored key messages for each audience group.
- Recommended channels (email campaigns, blog articles, social media assets, partner outreach).
- Suggested timelines and content formats (infographics, summary briefs, newsletters).

## Impact & Value

This project strengthened clarity around One Acre Fund's 2023 outcomes and created a concise communication pathway for increasing visibility, stakeholder engagement, and donor support.

It also demonstrates:

- Ability to analyze nonprofit impact through quantitative and qualitative lenses.
- Skill in translating data into accessible, compelling narratives.
- Capacity to combine research with strategic communication.
- Experience creating professional, publication-ready documentation.

projects.title: Sustainability Assessment of Lithium Mining in the Atacama Desert
projects.description: Evaluating environmental, social, and governance trade-offs of lithium extraction in the global energy transition.

drawer.subtitle: Balancing the Global Energy Transition with Local Environmental Justice

meta.label: Project Type
meta.value: Multidisciplinary Case Study — Sustainability & Resource Governance

drawer.body:
## Context

Lithium is a critical mineral powering the global transition to renewable energy and electric vehicles. Over half of the world's lithium reserves are concentrated in the "Lithium Triangle" of Chile, Argentina, and Bolivia. This case study examined lithium brine extraction in the Salar de Atacama, Northern Chile — one of the driest regions on Earth — where large-scale evaporation ponds are used to extract lithium for battery production.

While lithium supports decarbonization globally, its extraction raises urgent concerns around water depletion, ecosystem damage, and indigenous community rights. This project explored whether growing lithium demand can be satisfied without causing environmental and social harm.

## Project Goals

1. **Evaluate Environmental Sustainability**

  Assess water consumption, brine depletion, chemical processing, and ecological impacts associated with lithium extraction in arid ecosystems.
2. **Examine Social & Ethical Implications**

  Analyze impacts on indigenous Atacameño communities, including water access conflicts, land rights, and stakeholder inequality.
3. **Assess Economic & Policy Drivers**

  Understand global lithium demand linked to electric vehicle batteries and evaluate governance structures regulating extraction in Chile.
4. **Develop Balanced Sustainability Recommendations**

  Propose strategies to reconcile climate transition objectives with local environmental protection and social justice.

## Project Context

Lithium in Chile is extracted from underground brine reservoirs through solar evaporation ponds — a process requiring significant water withdrawal in a region already experiencing extreme water scarcity.

Key challenges investigated included:

- Over-extraction of brine beyond recharge capacity
- Declining groundwater levels affecting agriculture and biodiversity
- Increased socio-environmental conflicts
- Limited transparency in hydrological monitoring
- Tension between national economic growth and local sustainability

The project incorporated real-world stakeholder perspectives, including mining companies, indigenous communities, NGOs, and Chilean government agencies.

## Technical & Sustainability Scope

The assessment covered brine extraction and evaporation processes, water balance analysis and recharge limitations, chemical treatment and waste management, Life Cycle Thinking and sustainability trade-offs, and climate adaptation risks.

Frameworks applied: UN SDGs mapping, Stakeholder Power–Interest analysis, ESG evaluation, and sustainability trade-off analysis.

## Key Contributions

1. **Environmental Risk Analysis**

  Evaluated hydrological stress and long-term ecosystem impacts associated with lithium brine extraction.
2. **Stakeholder Negotiation & Governance Assessment**

  Participated in multi-party negotiation exercises to reconcile competing interests between government, corporations, and local communities.
3. **Sustainability Trade-off Evaluation**

  Assessed the paradox between global decarbonization benefits and localized environmental degradation.
4. **Strategic Recommendations**

  Proposed improved monitoring transparency, stronger community consultation mechanisms, and resource efficiency strategies.

## Impact

This case study highlighted the complexity of responsible mineral extraction in the energy transition. It demonstrated that sustainability in critical mineral supply chains requires integrated environmental governance, community-inclusive decision-making, transparent water monitoring, and balanced economic development.

The project strengthened my ability to analyze ESG risks in resource-intensive industries and evaluate sustainability beyond surface-level climate benefits.

projects.title: Advanced Bio-Butanol Production From Corn Stover
projects.description: Designing a full-scale biochemical process for sustainable ABE fermentation.

drawer.subtitle: Designing a full-scale biochemical process for sustainable ABE fermentation.
drawer.body:
## Context

Bio-butanol has emerged as a promising low-carbon alternative to petrochemical fuels, offering higher energy density and compatibility with existing fuel infrastructure. However, large-scale production faces challenges related to feedstock availability, process efficiency, and solvent recovery. This design project explored the full transformation of corn stover, a widely available agricultural residue, into acetone-butanol-ethanol (ABE) solvents through an integrated biochemical pathway.

Our team developed a full industrial process design covering pretreatment, hydrolysis, fermentation, product recovery, waste treatment, and heat integration. The goal was to determine whether a corn-stover-to-butanol system could be technically feasible, economically competitive, and environmentally sustainable at industrial scale.

## Research Objectives

1. **Develop a Complete Process Model**

  A full mass- and energy-balanced process model was developed, integrating mechanical size reduction, alkaline hydrolysis and enzymatic saccharification, Clostridium-based ABE fermentation, and solvent separation via distillation. The model quantified material flows, utility demands, and performance metrics across all unit operations.
2. **Detailed Process Flow Diagram (PFD)**

  A comprehensive PFD was constructed to capture biomass conversion pathways, fermenter configurations, product-recovery sequences, and waste-handling and heat-integration systems. This diagram formed the basis for equipment sizing and all downstream design calculations.
3. **Techno-Economic Assessment (TEA)**

  Capital and operating costs were evaluated across feedstock logistics, fermentation performance, distillation energy demand, and equipment and utilities. This assessment established the overall financial viability of the process and enabled comparison with conventional petrochemical butanol production.
4. **Environmental & Sustainability Assessment**

  Environmental performance was assessed through energy requirements, process emissions, wastewater impacts, and opportunities for heat recovery and waste valorisation, providing an integrated view of the system's sustainability profile.

## Key Findings

1. **Technical Performance**
  - Using 211,338 tonnes of corn stover annually enabled production of 40,000 tonnes of butanol, plus ethanol and acetone by-products.
  - Saccharification and fermentation achieved high sugar-conversion rates under optimised conditions.
  - Integrated distillation successfully recovered solvents to marketable purity.
2. **Energy & Process Efficiency**
  - Heat integration strategies (e.g., waste-heat recovery) significantly reduced steam demand.
  - Fermenter design and improved sugar availability enhanced solvent productivity.
  - Equipment sizing and recycle loops proved scalable and industrially realistic.
3. **Economic & Environmental Insights**

  The proposed system demonstrated potential profitability with competitive operating costs, reduced environmental burden compared to fossil-derived butanol, and strong improvement pathways including enhanced microbial yields and alternative separation technologies.

## Overall Impact

This design project demonstrated that corn-stover-based butanol production can be technically feasible, economically competitive, and environmentally advantageous. The system we developed provides a credible blueprint for scaling bio-based fuels and advancing the circular bioeconomy.

The work highlights how agricultural residues can be converted into high-value chemicals through integrated, sustainable, and systems-driven engineering design.

projects.title: Optimizing Plastic Waste Recovery at Skelmersdale Recycling Plant
projects.description: Streamlining processes and communication workflows to improve plastic recovery outcomes.

drawer.subtitle: Streamlining process and communication workflows to improve plastic recovery outcomes.
drawer.body:
## Context

Plastic waste is one of the most pressing environmental challenges in the United Kingdom. To meet rising demand for high-quality recycled materials and reduce reliance on landfills, Viridor—one of the UK's leading recycling companies—launched the Viridor Optical Sorting Equipment (VOSE) project.

This case study examines how advanced optical sorting technology can transform recycling operations at the Skelmersdale recycling facility—blending engineering, project management, sustainability strategy, and change management to deliver a more efficient and scalable plastic-sorting system.

## Project Goals

1. **Enhance Plastic Sorting Efficiency**

  Increase HDPE recycling rates at the Skelmersdale plant from 50% to 70% by implementing advanced, automated sorting technology.
2. **Integrate High-Tech Optical Sorting**

  Install a Buhler Sortex optical sorting system capable of producing over 500 tonnes of HDPE per month and supporting long-term processing goals of 100,000 tonnes of plastic annually by 2022.
3. **Strengthen Project Management Processes**

  Apply rigorous project management methodologies, including risk management, scope definition, Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), scheduling & critical path analysis, stakeholder engagement, and change management.

## Project Context

Viridor manages recycling operations for over 100 UK local authorities, but manual sorting methods were becoming inefficient and unable to meet quality requirements for recycled plastics.

The VOSE project—valued at £1.5 million and expected to run for 23 months—aimed to reduce manual sorting, increase accuracy in HDPE separation, improve throughput and consistency, and support market demand for sustainable materials. To deliver the technology, Viridor collaborated with Buhler Sortex, a Swiss company specializing in high-precision sorting systems, using a matrix project structure with 35–45 personnel.

Milestones: Design completion (May 2019), Equipment assembly (September 2019), Testing & validation (December 2019), Full operational deployment (end of 2020).

## Key Project Management Contributions

1. **Project Scoping & Definition** — Defined clear project boundaries to prevent scope creep; established SMART objectives such as HDPE output targets and annual recycling volumes.
2. **Project Charter Development** — Formalized deliverables, schedules, stakeholder roles, resource allocation, and risk thresholds to guide execution from initiation to completion.
3. **Work Breakdown Structure & Scheduling**
  - Created a detailed WBS from high-level phases down to individual work packages.
  - Managed dependencies between mechanical installation, software development, and system integration.
  - Applied parallel task scheduling to minimize delays.
4. **Risk Management**
  - Identified 10 major risks, including procurement delays, hardware misalignment, and software-integration challenges.
  - Built a risk register with likelihood, impact, and mitigation strategies.
  - Calculated Expected Monetary Value (EMV) for critical risks.
  - Used probability–impact matrices to prioritize interventions.
5. **Change Management** — Applied Kotter's 8-step model to support the transition from manual sorting to automated systems; addressed worker concerns about job security and new processes.
6. **Stakeholder Engagement** — Mapped stakeholders using the Power–Interest Matrix; managed communication strategies for high-power roles and kept executives informed without over-engagement.
7. **Monitoring & Control** — Maintained performance baselines, conducted milestone tracking, and ensured corrective measures were applied proactively.
8. **Sustainability & Continuous Improvement** — Identified long-term reinforcement measures to ensure the new technology delivers sustained environmental and operational benefits beyond project closure.

## Impact

The VOSE project provided a scalable model for modernizing recycling operations across the UK. It demonstrated how advanced sorting technology—combined with strong project management and change leadership—can dramatically improve recycling rates, reduce manual labor dependence, and support national sustainability goals.

projects.title: Utilization of Nigerian Carbon Black-Based Formulations in Printing Ink and Shoe Polish Production
projects.description: Investigating circular-economy innovation through local carbon black applications.

drawer.subtitle: Investigating circular-economy innovation through local carbon black applications.
drawer.body:
## Context

Nigeria produces millions of waste tires annually, many of which end up in landfills or are burned, releasing harmful emissions. At the same time, manufacturers of printing ink and shoe polish rely heavily on imported carbon black—a petroleum-based input that increases costs and environmental impact.

This research project explored the feasibility of using locally sourced carbon black—derived from waste-tire pyrolysis—as a sustainable alternative for ink and polish production. The work addressed both product performance and environmental impact, contributing to circular-economy innovation in Nigeria's materials industry.

## Research Objectives

1. **Develop Sustainable Material Formulations**

  Create printing-ink and shoe-polish formulations using Nigerian carbon black to replace non-local, non-renewable additives.
2. **Optimize Material Ratios**

  Design experimental ratios for waxes (paraffin vs. beeswax) and resin-based additives to evaluate performance, stability, and sustainability.
3. **Conduct Laboratory Testing & Chemical Analysis**

  Assess viscosity, pH, density, ash content, moisture content, drying time, and absorbance across multiple reagent combinations.
4. **Evaluate Environmental Impact**

  Assess the production process to identify opportunities for waste reduction and improved energy efficiency.

## Key Findings

1. **Printing Ink Formulation**
  - Phenol resin improved drying rate but reduced pH at higher concentrations.
  - Lead acetate affected viscosity and absorbance properties.
  - Optimal formulations balanced drying time, stability, and environmental safety.
2. **Shoe Polish Formulation**
  - Higher paraffin wax produced a more viscous, solid polish; increased ash content and pH.
  - Higher beeswax produced a creamier polish; decreased ash content and pH.
  - Optimal wax ratios produced polish with desirable texture, shine, and durability.
3. **Sustainability Benefits**
  - Nigerian carbon black offers high-quality, performance-ready alternatives to imported inputs.
  - Supports local circular-economy development.
  - Reduces environmental burden from tire waste.
  - Lowers production costs for manufacturers.

## Impact

This research demonstrated that Nigerian carbon black offers viable, environmentally beneficial potential for industrial ink and polish production. The findings support local circular-economy development, lower production costs for manufacturers, reduced environmental burden from tire waste, and pathways for greener, locally sourced materials in chemical manufacturing.

projects.title: Production Design for 100 Tonnes/Day of Sugar from Sugar Cane
projects.description: Designing a sustainable, large-scale sugar production process.

drawer.subtitle: Engineering a full-scale industrial process for refined sugar from sugarcane.

meta.label: Award
meta.value: Third Place – NSChE 2017 National Students' Annual Project Design Competition

drawer.body:
## Context

Sugar production remains a critical agro-industrial process across emerging economies, with increasing demand for higher-efficiency plants, better resource utilization, and improved product quality. Traditional sugar manufacturing methods face challenges related to extraction efficiency, energy intensity, waste handling, and process optimization.

This group design project focused on developing a complete industrial plant capable of producing 100 tonnes/day of refined white sugar (99.9% purity) from locally grown Saccharum officinarum sugarcane. The design incorporated milling, clarification, evaporation, crystallisation, centrifugation, affination, melting, decolourisation, drying, and bagasse-based cogeneration. The objective was to deliver a technically sound, economically viable, and environmentally sustainable plant configuration suited to Nigerian agricultural and industrial conditions.

## Research Objectives

1. **Develop a Complete Process Model**

  We built a fully mass- and energy-balanced model covering all units: cane preparation, milling, lime clarification, multiple-effect evaporation, crystallisation, centrifugation, refining, and drying. The model quantified sucrose recovery efficiencies, bagasse generation, water usage, steam demand, and overall plant yield.
2. **Construct a Detailed Process Flow Diagram (PFD)**

  A full PFD was produced, mapping juice extraction, purification steps, evaporation stages, crystal growth, molasses separation, colour removal, and sugar drying. This diagram served as the basis for equipment sizing, heat-duty calculations, and utility integration.
3. **Perform a Techno-Economic Assessment (TEA)**

  Capital and operating costs were evaluated across milling equipment, evaporation trains, crystallisers, boilers, dryers, labour, and utilities. The TEA established the financial feasibility of the 100-TPD plant and highlighted cost drivers such as steam generation and crystallisation energy requirements.
4. **Conduct an Environmental & Sustainability Assessment**

  The project examined waste streams (bagasse, filter cake, molasses), energy recovery via bagasse-fired boilers, process emissions, and opportunities for resource optimization. Bagasse cogeneration was shown to significantly reduce external energy needs and improve plant sustainability.

## Key Findings

1. **Technical Performance**
  - Milling efficiency of 95% enabled strong sucrose extraction.
  - Clarification achieved 96% impurity removal, improving downstream evaporation.
  - Multiple-effect evaporation (triple effect) reduced steam consumption while achieving target syrup concentrations (~60% solids).
  - Crystallisation and centrifugation produced refined sugar with final moisture reduced to 0.2% after drying.
2. **Energy & Process Efficiency**
  - Bagasse (~30% of cane input) supplied sufficient fuel for boiler and steam generation.
  - Heat integration across clarifiers, evaporators, and crystallisers minimized external heat demand.
  - Mechanical and thermal design ensured realistic industrial operability.
3. **Economic & Environmental Insights**

  The proposed plant demonstrated feasibility under Nigerian agricultural conditions, reduced reliance on fossil fuels due to bagasse-based cogeneration, scalable design adaptable to larger production capacities, and opportunities for by-product valorisation (molasses, filter cake, bagasse).

## Overall Impact

This project produced a complete engineering design for a sugar production facility capable of delivering 100 tonnes/day of refined white sugar, using locally available feedstock and sustainable process integration. The work showcases how agricultural value chains can be strengthened through efficient process engineering, energy recovery, and optimized chemical operations.

The project received Third Place at the 2017 NSChE National Student Project Design Competition, recognizing its technical depth, process integration, and industrial relevance.
